title: Why Are There Balls on Power Lines?
description:
Drive near an airport or across a big river valley and you may see giant colored balls hanging on power lines, orange, white and yellow, high above the ground. They look like toys someone threw up there. They are not. Each one may be saving a pilot's life. Today, eleven parts of a high voltage power line, and why each one exists, starting with those balls.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:09 1. The colored balls
2:22 2. The little dumbbells
3:36 3. The spacers between wires
4:50 4. The stack of discs
5:58 5. The metal rings at the ends
7:06 6. The wire on the very top
8:10 7. The spirals for birds
9:15 8. The barbed panels on the legs
10:16 9. The man on the live wire
11:27 10. The wire that sags
12:34 11. The giant towers
13:43 The verdict

Sources:
- Aerial marker balls (placement, 36-inch / 20-inch sizes, orange/white/yellow alternating): FAA Advisory Circular 70/7460-1 "Obstruction Marking and Lighting" https://www.faa.gov/ ; Wikipedia, "Aerial marker spheres" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_marker_spheres
- Stockbridge damper and aeolian vibration (George H. Stockbridge, 1920s patent): Wikipedia, "Stockbridge damper" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockbridge_damper
- Bundle conductors, spacers and corona discharge: Wikipedia, "Overhead power line" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overhead_power_line ; Wikipedia, "Corona discharge" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corona_discharge
- Insulator strings (disc count vs voltage, creepage distance, toughened glass shattering): Wikipedia, "Insulator (electricity)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insulator_(electricity)
- Corona / grading rings: Wikipedia, "Corona ring" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corona_ring
- Shield wires and OPGW: Wikipedia, "Optical ground wire" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_ground_wire
- Bird diverters and collision reduction: APLIC (Avian Power Line Interaction Committee), "Reducing Avian Collisions with Power Lines" (2012) https://www.aplic.org/
- Live-line work from helicopters, bare-hand method, Faraday suits: Wikipedia, "Live-line working" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live-line_working
- 2003 Northeast blackout (14 August 2003, sagging lines into trees in Ohio, alarm failure, ~50 million people): US-Canada Power System Outage Task Force Final Report (2004) ; Wikipedia, "Northeast blackout of 2003" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeast_blackout_of_2003
- High voltage transmission losses (I^2 R) and three-phase power: Wikipedia, "Electric power transmission" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_power_transmission
